# Stack Fingerprint

> Analyze any GitHub repository to identify its tech stack and generate an embeddable SVG card for your README.

## Docs
- [Stack Fingerprint](https://stackfingerprint.vercel.app/): Paste a GitHub repo URL, detect its stack and configure the card.
- [Card API](https://stackfingerprint.vercel.app/api/card?repo=OWNER/REPO): SVG card endpoint. Options: theme, layout, size, categoryFilter, path (monorepo subfolder).
- [README](https://github.com/mattqdev/stackfingerprint#readme): Full usage, themes and options.
- [GitHub Action](https://github.com/mattqdev/stackfingerprint-action): Commits an up-to-date stack card to your repo's README.

## Blog
- [How Stack Fingerprint detects 200+ technologies with one GitHub API call](https://stackfingerprint.vercel.app/blog/how-stack-detection-works): Inside the scanner: one recursive Git Trees request, file signals, dependency signals, dev-only tagging, and why every icon has to be inlined as a data URI for GitHub to render it.
- [Automate your README's tech stack with GitHub Actions](https://stackfingerprint.vercel.app/blog/automate-readme-stack-card-github-action): Generate an up-to-date tech stack card on every push and commit it to your repo, so your README never depends on a third-party image server. Setup, inputs and monorepo tips.
- [How to add a tech stack section to your GitHub README (2026 guide)](https://stackfingerprint.vercel.app/blog/add-tech-stack-to-github-readme): Three ways to show what your project is built with: hand-made shields.io badges, a live auto-detected stack card, or a card committed by a GitHub Action. Pros, cons and copy-paste snippets.

## Technologies
- [Supported technologies](https://stackfingerprint.vercel.app/tech): Every framework, language, database and tool the scanner detects, with the files and dependencies used for each.
